method: Near-duplicate photographs are found with a 64-bit perceptual hash and a 64-bit difference hash computed on grayscale thumbnails; two images are near-duplicates when both Hamming distances are at most 6 bits, and near-duplicates are merged into groups. The analysis is repeated on partitions in which every group lies entirely in one split (70/15/15 within each class). To test whether the color evidence comes from the background, the 57 color features are recomputed on the leaf only and on the background only, using a leaf mask from Otsu thresholding of saturation; a color classifier trained on background-only features measures how much class information the background carries, and the whole analysis is repeated with the leaf-only color expert.
dup_sentence: Perceptual hashing finds 39 groups of near-duplicate photographs covering 78 images (largest group 2; 1 with conflicting labels); in the fixed partition 10 test images have a near-duplicate in the training or validation split.
text: **Near-duplicates.** On 10 near-duplicate-aware partitions the baseline reaches 96.97 ± 0.35% Macro-F1, the raw weights are consistent with the single-group criterion in 3/10 partitions and the margin contribution in 10/10 (10/10 without labels). **Background.** A color classifier trained on background pixels only reaches 84.39 ± 0.96% Macro-F1 (the first 10 partitions), against 87.52 ± 0.59% on leaf pixels only and 95.42 ± 0.37% on the whole image. With the leaf-only color expert (87.52% Macro-F1, sharpness 0.874) the raw weights are consistent in 5/10 partitions and the margin contribution in 10/10.
